increment_status: bounded native foundation implemented; focused Linux Debug/strict acceptance passed; independent Wrench review pending
changes: Added include/void/console.hpp and src/runtime/console.cpp to the existing Runtime archive. No source endpoint token or public console API.
Lazily published per-Runtime Context sessions over one persistent native process Streams state; independent injected Streams/Adapter contexts for tests.

Borrowed standard endpoints retain distinct role identities and independent snapshot classification. POSIX fstat/isatty and Windows GetStdHandle/GetFileType/positive GetConsoleMode; no closing/duplication/hidden terminal or mode/code-page changes.

One shared input gate and one shared stdout/stderr gate; separate per-Runtime closing/admission and standard C++ cancellation tokens. Queued operations reject; granted leases retain state until safely released.
NativeSafe/unattached gate/wait/drain requirements, thread-bound leases, input-before-output nesting and recursive/self-drain rejection; immutable endpoint metadata uses no GC storage.

Runtime lookup prepares native state outside the GC mutex and rechecks shutdown before installing a winner. Runtime close cancels/drains before existing native shutdown and heap teardown; existing participant/handle lifetime rules remain.
Native-only destructors release owned state while still NativeSafe, including final host references dropped during Managed execution. No executable/source callback resource registry.

strict_sanitizers.configuration: RelWithDebInfo, pinned LLVM/Clang 19.1.7, existing RTTI-off vptr exclusion
strict_sanitizers.execution: Outside restricted ptrace runner for actual LeakSanitizer checking. No sanitizer/leak error. Expected fatal-invariant children retain their existing exit-79 handlers and native leak-negative controls; no assertions or sanitizer options disabled.

lifecycle_guarantees: Process Streams remains shared between Runtime lifetimes; closing a Runtime changes only its own Session. Host mutation/closure of live borrowed standard endpoints is outside the embedding contract.
Endpoint role identity is independent of destination equality; all stdout/stderr records share one native gate, including aliases of a redirected file.

A granted native operation pins its Session, adapter and coordinator. Runtime close signals cancellation and waits for admitted operations; queued calls wake and reject. Concurrent closes are idempotent.
Standalone Context destruction signals cancellation without draining itself. Outstanding Operation leases retain all native state; thread-bound operation release completes native cleanup.
Drain attempts from the owning operation reject before Runtime admission is changed. Closed acquisition reports Closed even when another session owns the same gate.

Cancellation handlers are native signal-only callbacks scoped within operation lifetime; no source/GC-managed callbacks or managed object views are stored. Step 24 must translate tokens into per-request OS wakeups, cancelling only owned requests.
Native resources cannot be transferred from raw source integers: no source console types/operations are introduced. C++ Adapter injection is a trusted embedding boundary.

No native stream wait holds the Runtime GC mutex. Existing Runtime participants/handles must still be drained before Runtime destruction; this is not permission to destroy beneath attached Managed code.

Linux: stdin pipe, stdout file, stderr PTY
stdin PTY, stdout/stderr one shared redirected file
Unicode/NUL payload remains available to host reads after Runtime teardown
